title: Market Cartography: Use-case-led Competitive Signal Pipeline
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Objective: Build a repeatable, use-case-first pipeline that continuously maps open and commercial model releases to prioritized Redwood customer use-cases, surfaces competitive signals (latency/cost/feature changes, licenses, quantization support), and produces actionable alerts and a living dashboard for PMs/PMMs/SEs.

Background: Current model tracking is ad hoc: spreadsheets, one-off PR notes, and defensive signal hunting. We need a systematic approach that ties model-level changes to product impact (e.g., a new sparse attention variant could change cost/latency tradeoffs for Redwood Dedicated customers). This ticket covers the PM scope: taxonomy, signal types, scoring rubric, validation plan, and handoff to Eng/Research for implementation of ingestion pipelines and dashboards.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: taxonomy design, prioritized use-case list, scoring rubric, alerting rules, dashboard wireframes, vendor/OSS release scraping spec, and acceptance criteria.
- Out of scope: building the crawler/ETL, model benchmarking infra, or the runtime router changes (these are separate eng tickets).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented taxonomy (CSV + Confluence doc) mapping 25+ representative Redwood product use-cases to model capability vectors and compatibility constraints.
2) A signal taxonomy and scoring rubric (CSV) that converts raw events (release notes, license changes, perf benchmarks) into an impact score [0-100] and recommended action (monitor, evaluate, onboard, block).
3) Dashboard wireframes and user stories reviewed and approved by Console PM, DS lead, and a Solutions Engineer.
4) Three example alert rules described and validated against historical events (linked).
5) Handoff doc with clear data contracts for Eng/Research to implement ingestion + model evaluation jobs.
approach:
1) Kickoff and rapid research (2 weeks): interviews with SEs, 6 field customers, Console PM, and 3 eng leads to enumerate high-value use-cases and current failure modes.
2) Taxonomy draft: produce a use-case matrix (rows: use-cases; columns: capability-attributes like low-latency, streaming stability, structured output, hallucination sensitivity, quantization friendliness, license constraints).
3) Signal design: enumerate sources (GitHub releases, model zoo metadata, arXiv/tech blogs, model card updates, benchmark feeds, community forums). Map each source to parsers and a confidence weight.
4) Scoring: define heuristics and thresholding for impact levels; validate with 10 historical events.
5) Dashboard and alerting: create wireframes and a prioritized backlog of signals to ingest first.
6) Handoff: produce Confluence spec, example JSON event shape, and high-priority test cases for Research to benchmark.
risks: Signal noise: noisy release notes may produce false positives
Data coverage: important proprietary vendor changes may be behind paywalls
Alignment: taxonomy needs cross-org buy-in or it will be ignored
Operational cost: naive crawling/benchmarking will exceed budget
